messages:
maria: heads up — running a long-context chat workload and KV cache memory steadily grows over time (no bound). started after the batching/slot-reuse change we merged last week.

josh: rough numbers? how much over what time?

maria: ~6GB -> ~28GB over ~3h on a 16GB process with 1M token stream. flamegraphs point at kv lookup/alloc churn. no OOM but sustained growth.

kevin: which change specifically? my batching patch touched reuse and free-list behavior.

maria: @kevin seems correlated. quick log excerpt shows reused block ids with mismatched token seq tags: 
```
[kv] checkout block_id=1024 tag_seq=120 alloc_gen=5 current_req_seq=123
[kv] checkout block_id=1024 tag_seq=120 -> data looks stale (token 800k)
[kv] allocated block_id=1024 gen=6 zeroed=false
```

alice: that looks like a generational/tag desync — we expect checkout to validate tag_seq == current_req_seq before returning a block. if false, should evict/zero.

josh: can you dump the free-list state and gen counters when it happens? a small repro would help.

maria: putting a repro together now. quick script: long_reuse_runner --model small --ctx 64k --threads 8 --requests 10k (each request appends 4k tokens). I can share CI harness.

perf-bot: perf viz: https://perf.redwood/test/1772456789/kv_frag_long_context flamegraph shows hot path in kv_checkout -> memcpy.

kevin: digging into my diff — I optimized for fast-path reuse by skipping tag validation for non-eviction paths to reduce latency. looks like a race: if eviction occurs concurrently and increments the gen, checkout can read stale state and return a block before tag updated.

alice: so cross-request contamination risk + fragmentation because we reuse partially-filled blocks without resetting their metadata. fix options: (1) re-introduce atomic tag check on checkout, (2) bump gen on any reuse and zero memory, (3) avoid reuse for long-context workloads (slow path).

maria: temporary mitigation: add a debug assert to detect tag mismatch and force eviction. I've reproduced locally after forcing higher contention.

josh: can you paste the exact assert/log you added?

maria: added: `if (block.tag_seq != req.seq) { log.warn("kv stale reuse block=%d tag=%d req=%d", id, block.tag_seq, req.seq); evict(block); }` — triggered after ~20k requests in repro.

kevin: ok I can push a patch to restore atomic check + a perf counter for tag-failures. will also add optional zeroing on allocate behind a flag.

perf-bot: regression detector flagged this as a correctness issue (ranked high) and linked PRs that touched reuse heuristics in the last 14 days.

alice: test plan: 1) small unit that flips gen and tries concurrent checkout, 2) stress test harness with long_reuse_runner under CI job, 3) add mem-usage assertion to nightly.

maria: opened issue #1324 with logs/repro and attached perf link. assigning to @kevin for fix, @josh for adding tests, @maria for repro harness.

kevin: starting PR now. I will keep the micro-optimizations behind a runtime flag until we validate.

sre-bot: canary cluster restarted with kv allocator patch reverted on canary nodes to stop growth. will monitor metrics for 1 hour.

josh: thanks everyone — please post GH PR link when ready and drop the perf numbers.

maria: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 — main change is atomic tag check + counter + optional zeroing. verifying perf impact now.

kevin: local perf shows ~1.8% p99 latency hit on microbenchmarks when atomic check is enabled, but memory growth stops. worth it for correctness.

alice: we can A/B the flag in staging and see real workload impact.

maria: leaving the repro harness and a nightly job to exercise long contexts. will follow up with regression numbers. :white_check_mark:
